course_name_original: Climatización y Ahorro Energético en Edificios
course_name_en: Air Conditioning and Energy Saving in Buildings
prerequisites: Having passed the subjects corresponding to the basic Physics and Mathematics, Thermotechnics and Thermal Engineering competencies. Specifically, the prior requirements would be at least:

From PHYSICS: Concepts of energy, power, mass, absolute and relative pressure, temperature, density, specific volume, specific heats, enthalpy. Unit systems for each of the above concepts and unit changes for the International System, and others.

From MATHEMATICS: Interpolation of one and several variables. Partial derivatives. Gradient of a scalar field. Integrals. Concept of limit. Boundary conditions. Laplace and Fourier transforms. Resolution of systems of linear and non-linear equations. Matrix resolution of systems of equations.
From THERMOTECHNICS and THERMAL ENGINEERING: Concepts of energy, thermodynamic processes, thermodynamics of humid air.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design air conditioning installations.
Knowledge of different energy saving alternatives in buildings.
Knowledge for designing passive building conditioning techniques.
Knowledge of current regulations on energy efficiency in buildings and use of simulation and energy certification tools.

PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 2. Air Conditioning Regulations
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 3. Introduction to Psychrometry
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 4. Thermal Comfort
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 5. Thermal Loads
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 6. Heating
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 7. Thermal Analysis
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 8. Basic Air Cycle
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 9. Air Conditioning Systems
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 10. Air Distribution in Premises
PART I: AIR CONDITIONING INSTALLATIONS - Topic 11. Calculation and Design of Ducts
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 1. Global vision of energy: sources, supply, utilization. Energy transformations.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 2. Current situation of energy consumption. Primary and final energy consumption data; analysis and trends.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 3. Energy efficiency. Technologies involving energy saving.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 4. Energy saving in processes and equipment.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 5. Energy aspects of the Technical Building Code (CTE), and building energy certification.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 6. Passive techniques for building conditioning.
PART II: ENERGY SAVING IN BUILDINGS - Topic 7. Energy management in buildings.
assessment_rules: The course is assessed entirely through practical work, which can be individual or group-based, accounting for 100% of the final grade.
